title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #3

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction lies between north and west? (1 mark)
   A. South-east
   B. South-west
   C. North-east
   D. North-west

2. Where does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. In the west
   B. In the south
   C. In the north
   D. In the east

3. Which country lies to the south of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Ethiopia
   B. Tanzania
   C. South Sudan
   D. Uganda

4. Which country lies to the west of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Ethiopia
   B. Uganda
   C. Tanzania
   D. Somalia

5. Why is it useful to know the size of a county? (1 mark)
   A. It tells us the price of food
   B. It tells us what to eat
   C. It tells us the weather
   D. It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics

6. What do we call a place where a river falls over a cliff? (1 mark)
   A. Valley
   B. Plain
   C. Plateau
   D. Waterfall

7. Lake Nakuru is famous for which birds? (1 mark)
   A. Owls
   B. Flamingos
   C. Ostriches
   D. Eagles

8. Which of these is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A lake
   B. A bridge
   C. A road
   D. A school

9. Which physical feature helps people to catch fish? (1 mark)
   A. A plateau
   B. A lake
   C. A plain
   D. A hill

10. On a weather chart, which symbol usually means a sunny day? (1 mark)
   A. A raindrop
   B. A sun
   C. A wind arrow
   D. A cloud

11. Which season is best for planting most crops? (1 mark)
   A. Dry season
   B. Hot season
   C. Cold season
   D. Rainy season

12. Gede Ruins are near which coastal town? (1 mark)
   A. Watamu
   B. Nyeri
   C. Kisumu
   D. Nakuru

13. Fort Jesus is found in which town? (1 mark)
   A. Eldoret
   B. Nakuru
   C. Kisumu
   D. Mombasa

14. Which of these is not a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A cultural centre
   B. A museum
   C. A monument
   D. A natural river

15. Who built Fort Jesus? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody built it
   B. The Kenyan government in 1990
   C. The British in 1950
   D. The Portuguese

16. What is harambee? (1 mark)
   A. Working together to solve a problem
   B. A school subject
   C. A type of crop
   D. A kind of market

17. What does interdependence mean? (1 mark)
   A. People doing everything themselves
   B. People living alone
   C. People fighting
   D. People needing and helping each other

18. Which of these is not a reason for crowded areas? (1 mark)
   A. Very little rain and no water
   B. Fertile soil
   C. Good roads
   D. Jobs in a town

19. Why do many people live near rivers and lakes? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers are always dry
   B. Rivers are dangerous
   C. Water is available for drinking and farming
   D. Lakes have no fish

20. What do we call an area where few people live in a large space? (1 mark)
   A. Densely populated
   B. Busy
   C. Crowded
   D. Sparsely populated

21. Why must a key be included on a dot map? (1 mark)
   A. So that people know what each dot stands for
   B. So that it looks old
   C. So that colours are hidden
   D. So that the map is longer

22. What is culture? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of weather
   B. A kind of animal
   C. The way of life of a community
   D. A type of road

23. What is a gallery walk? (1 mark)
   A. A cooking lesson
   B. A kind of assembly
   C. A race
   D. Walking round to look at displayed work

24. Why is it important to check facts before telling your school's history? (1 mark)
   A. So that nobody listens
   B. So that it is funny
   C. So that the story is longer
   D. So that what you tell is true

25. Which of these is a human resource? (1 mark)
   A. A skilled farmer
   B. A lake
   C. A forest
   D. A mineral

26. What is a budget? (1 mark)
   A. A crop
   B. A type of tool
   C. A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   D. A game

27. What should be done with profit from a school project? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Throw it away
   C. Share it secretly
   D. Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books

28. What is an enterprise? (1 mark)
   A. A school rule
   B. A business activity to make goods or provide services
   C. A game
   D. A weather chart

29. Which action shows respect? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking desks
   B. Insulting classmates
   C. Greeting teachers politely
   D. Ignoring teachers

30. What is forgiveness? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping anger forever
   B. Ignoring the wrong
   C. Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you
   D. Punishing without listening

31. Which of these is a child right? (1 mark)
   A. To go to school
   B. To be beaten
   C. To work in a quarry
   D. To be married early

32. Which is an effect of child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. More friends
   B. Fear and lost education
   C. Better health
   D. Higher marks

33. Which of these is a democratic process in school? (1 mark)
   A. A bully choosing leaders
   B. Electing a class monitor by voting
   C. Ignoring pupils' ideas
   D. Punishing pupils who speak

34. What is a suggestion box used for? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   B. Storing books
   C. Keeping food
   D. Collecting rubbish

35. Why should voting be secret? (1 mark)
   A. So that nobody counts
   B. So that nobody can force how you vote
   C. So that the winner is hidden
   D. So that votes are lost

36. Which quality is important for a pupil leader? (1 mark)
   A. Selfishness
   B. Honesty
   C. Bullying
   D. Laziness

37. What does a class representative do? (1 mark)
   A. Punishes pupils
   B. Teaches lessons
   C. Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
   D. Cooks food

38. Who leads a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A footballer
   B. Clan elders
   C. A cook
   D. A bus driver

39. Which law created county governments in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A market rule
   B. The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   C. A church rule
   D. A school rule

40. Which of these is a national government service? (1 mark)
   A. Pre-primary schools
   B. Defence and security
   C. Cattle dips
   D. County markets

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State three benefits of interdependence in a county. (3 marks)

42. Explain the difference between a chief and a clan elder. (3 marks)

43. State three ways in which physical features are important to people. (3 marks)

44. Give three rules for using safe school transport. (3 marks)

45. State three duties of clan elders. (3 marks)

46. Draw a simple chart showing three workers, what each gives, and what each needs. (3 marks)

47. Explain how a county with a big lake and a dry plain could earn a living from both. (4 marks)

48. State three duties of a village elder. (3 marks)

49. Give four services provided by county governments. (4 marks)

50. Describe how an ordinary pupil can support the Children's Government. (3 marks)

51. Plan a class culture day. State five things you would include. (5 marks)

52. Explain why many factories are built near big towns. (3 marks)

53. Name the five countries that border Kenya. (5 marks)

54. Name four members of a typical Children's Government. (4 marks)

55. In a class election, Maria got 14 votes, Juma got 9 votes and 2 papers were spoilt. How many pupils voted? Who won? Show working. (3 marks)

56. A weather chart for a week shows: Mon sunny, Tue sunny, Wed rainy, Thu cloudy, Fri rainy, Sat sunny, Sun cloudy. How many days were sunny, rainy and cloudy? (3 marks)

57. Explain why buying votes with sweets is wrong. (3 marks)

58. How do you calculate profit? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — North-west
   North-west is between north and west.

2. D — In the east
   The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

3. B — Tanzania
   Tanzania borders Kenya to the south.

4. B — Uganda
   Uganda is Kenya's western neighbour.

5. D — It helps with planning services such as roads and clinics
   Planners need to know how much land there is to cover with services.

6. D — Waterfall
   A waterfall is where a river drops over a steep edge.

7. B — Flamingos
   Lake Nakuru is well known for flamingos.

8. A — A lake
   A lake is natural. The others are built by people.

9. B — A lake
   People fish in lakes, rivers and the ocean.

10. B — A sun
   A sun symbol shows sunny weather.

11. D — Rainy season
   Seeds need rain water to germinate and grow.

12. A — Watamu
   Gede Ruins are near Watamu in Kilifi County.

13. D — Mombasa
   Fort Jesus is a fort at Mombasa.

14. D — A natural river
   A river is a natural feature, not built by people.

15. D — The Portuguese
   The Portuguese built the fort more than 400 years ago.

16. A — Working together to solve a problem
   Harambee means pulling together.

17. D — People needing and helping each other
   Interdependence means we depend on each other.

18. A — Very little rain and no water
   Dryness with no water makes areas sparse.

19. C — Water is available for drinking and farming
   Water is a basic need.

20. D — Sparsely populated
   Sparse means thinly spread.

21. A — So that people know what each dot stands for
   Without a key we cannot read the dots.

22. C — The way of life of a community
   Culture is the way of life passed on from generation to generation.

23. D — Walking round to look at displayed work
   In a gallery walk pupils look at each other's displays.

24. D — So that what you tell is true
   History must be accurate.

25. A — A skilled farmer
   People's skills and labour are human resources.

26. C — A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   A budget plans money.

27. D — Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books
   Profit should be used openly and wisely.

28. B — A business activity to make goods or provide services
   Enterprises earn money by making goods or services.

29. C — Greeting teachers politely
   Polite greetings show respect.

30. C — Choosing to let go of anger against someone who wronged you
   Forgiveness ends quarrels.

31. A — To go to school
   Children have the right to education.

32. B — Fear and lost education
   Abuse harms the child's life.

33. B — Electing a class monitor by voting
   Voting gives everyone a say.

34. A — Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   It lets everyone share ideas.

35. B — So that nobody can force how you vote
   Secret voting protects free choice.

36. B — Honesty
   Leaders must be honest and fair.

37. C — Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
   Class representatives speak for their classmates.

38. B — Clan elders
   Clan elders lead the clan.

39. B — The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   The 2010 Constitution created counties.

40. B — Defence and security
   Defence is national.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: People get goods and services they cannot make, people help each other in trouble, and the county develops faster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A chief is appointed by the national government to lead a location. A clan elder is respected by a clan for age and wisdom and keeps customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give water, they provide fish and food, and they attract visitors. Accept farming land or electric power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use only transport approved by the school and parents, do not take lifts from strangers, and do not board overloaded vehicles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep customs, settle disputes and advise at ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer gives food and needs clothes; teacher gives learning and needs food; driver gives transport and needs repairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct row.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: People can fish in the lake and sell the fish. People on the dry plain can keep cattle and goats. Both bring food and income. The county can also use both for tourism.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome visitors, settle small quarrels and call meetings. Accept reporting problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health centres, county roads, pre-primary schools and markets. Accept cattle dips or water services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each service.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Vote for leaders, follow fair instructions, and give ideas through the class representative.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Traditional dress, foods to taste, songs and dances, artefacts on display, and stories told by elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Many customers live there. Workers live nearby. Roads and other services are available.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Somalia.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each country.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: President, deputy president, Speaker, and class representatives. Accept cabinet members or secretary.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each member.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 25 pupils voted. Maria won.
   Working / marking points: 14 + 9 + 2 = 25. 14 is more than 9, so Maria won. 1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the winner, 1 mark for showing working.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 sunny days, 2 rainy days and 2 cloudy days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count. Check: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 days.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is cheating, it makes the election unfair, and votes should be given freely on merit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Profit is found by subtracting the costs from the income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for costs from income.
